newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Qantas wins order to restrain job action.
newsitem.headline: Qantas wins order to restrain job action.

text.p: Qantas Airways Ltd said on Wednesday the Industrial Relations Commission had granted its application to restrain workers from taking further industrial action over plans to introduce competitive tendering for some ground services at Melbourne, Brisbane and Perth airports.

Australian Services Union (ASU) members employed as check-in, ticketing and customer service staff held unauthorised stop-work meetings on Wednesday, causing disruption to services, Qantas told the commission.
The commission resissued a direction that Qantas and the ASU establish a steering committee to oversee competitive tendering, Qantas said.
Both parties are to report back to the commission on June 10, the company said.
Qantas said it told the commission it was prepared to meet the ASU, provided the unionists withdrew the threat of industrial action.
The ASU earlier on Wednesday said about 1,000 of its members would be affected by competitive tendering.
Under the system, Qantas's internal units at airports would compete against outside companies for designated ground services, Qantas said.
Qantas earlier this month said it would retrench 132 staff and 53 apprentices from its engineering and maintenance division in order to improve productivity and efficiency.
The company is 25 percent owned by British Airways Plc .
